title: Replying to @Kate Reinking (and settling our beef!) #theatre #broadwa...
transcript: let this be a lesson to the people out there who act like the most boring Tony category is sound design of a play look at this comment from Kate and also this other comment on my video people feel passionately about this and for good reason so I've been thinking about this the last couple days and it's tricky and it also leads to a question that I genuinely would like to hear answers from from people in the industry but like: are sound designers in theater responsible for also mixing the sound? because I was kind of under the impression that they were two different jobs similar to how in film sound mixing and sound editing are two different roles but maybe I'm wrong about that and I would genuinely like to know but even if I am wrong about that I wanna add a bit of context to my comment to Kate where I said that I think Stereophonic is more of a feat of sound mixing than sound design I think part of that comment came from a bit of baggage and frustration that I have with the fact that a lot of people when they talk about sound design in theater really only ever talk about the mix “well I could hear the show so I guess the sound design was good!” or “well I missed some things so I guess the sound design was bad!” it feels like a little bit of a reductive view of the art form that I was the source of my knee jerk reaction but upon some reflection I can concede that especially in the case of Stereophonic specifically the sound mixing is so interwoven with the storytelling that even if I'm right about it being two different jobs (and again I don't know if I am right but even if I am) you kind of in this case have to consider the mixing part of the sound design so in that case yes I can acknowledge that a win in this category would be very well deserved HAVING SAID THAT…. the sound design in Grey House was freaking gorgeous it was so atmospheric and striking and effective and I would argue that in a certain sense the sound design in Grey House is just as important to the storytelling as in Stereophonic like not in as much of an overt, literal way sure, I get like it's in the title, fine but like in the sense that horror is a genre that is heavily reliant on sound to create its intended effect. as a little side note I also just wanna add that whenever someone brings up how difficult or technically impressive something is as an argument for why it should win an artistic award I'm always a little skeptical of that I tend to think that it should just go to what is the most effective in context but maybe that doesn't really apply here because in the case of Stereophonic it actually is very effective in context I'm just a little bit resistant to that line of reasoning. but like I said at the top either way you slice it I love that we can have such a passionate debate about this category specifically
